description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2094-2096 — CertificatePolicies is decoded via find_cert_ext (fail-open):
  `let cert_cp: Option<...CertificatePolicies> = find_cert_ext(cert, OID_CERTIFICATE_POLICIES);`

If CertificatePolicies is structurally present in a cert but its DER value is malformed, find_cert_ext returns None. This is then treated at line 2178-2181 as if the cert has NO certificate policies, which causes policy_tree to be set to None (§6.1.3(e): absence of CertificatePolicies → tree becomes NULL).

This means a malformed critical CertificatePolicies would:
1. Pass the check_critical_extensions (it's in HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS)
2. Be decoded via find_cert_ext as None
3. Be treated as 'no policies → tree = None'
4. If explicit_policy == 0, trigger PolicyViolation
5. If explicit_policy > 0, silently pass with NULL tree (no valid policies found)

For case 5: if initial_explicit_policy = false (the default), explicit_policy starts at n_u32+1 >> 0, so the chain may pass even though a critical CertificatePolicies extension was silently ignored.

Suggested fix: use try_find_cert_ext for CertificatePolicies (and probably PolicyMappings, PolicyConstraints). PolicyMappings already uses try_find_cert_ext (line 2316). The inconsistency between CertificatePolicies (fail-open) and PolicyMappings (fail-closed) is itself a finding.

P1 — malformed critical CertificatePolicies silently treated as absent, bypassing policy tree checks.
title: pkix-path: CertificatePolicies extension decoded fail-open via find_cert_ext
